name: Drum & Bass
summary: Drum & bass drums are built on the two-step skeleton - kick on beat 1 plus one syncopated kick, snares locked to 2 and 4 (halftime is the one exception, on beat 3 only) - with a ghost-snare micro-language between the backbeats descended straight from jungle's chopped breaks. The top end defines the subgenre: ride-driven 8ths for rollers, swung open hats for liquid, on-beat hats choking an offbeat skank for jump-up, and surgical 32nd micro-edits for neurofunk.

sounds.kick: Punchy programmed 909/808-style kick (sub-reinforced for jump-up/foghorn weight) sitting alongside, and often layered under, a chopped break kick inherited from jungle's Amen/Think source material.
sounds.snare: A composite snare/clap stack (909 body plus a sampled break snare for grit) carrying the 2-and-4 law, with dense low-velocity ghost hits between backbeats built from the same break-chopping vocabulary as jungle.
sounds.hats: Ride-driven 8ths for rollers, swung and open for liquid, tight and choking for jump-up, 32nd micro-edited for neurofunk - closed hats stay well under the kick/snare in velocity.
sounds.percussion: Conga/bongo hits and rim ticks lifted from the same funk/soul breaks jungle uses, filtered and processed into the halftime/autonomic and liquid palettes; neurofunk substitutes mechanical, edited percussion loops.
sounds.cymbals: A single crash marks phrase starts (dancefloor/jump-up); the ride is otherwise the only cymbal doing groove work.

machines: Roland TR-909 — kick body, ride, closed/open hat foundation across most subgenres
Roland TR-808 — sub kick layer, clap/snare doubling, cowbell-slot percussion
Akai S900 / S950 / S1000 — the same break-chopping and timestretch lineage jungle uses, still present in 'raw'/sample-based DnB
10 Most Iconic Amen Patterns / junglebreaks.co.uk / Neekeetone Jungle Breaks — Amen/Think/Apache source material for hybrid roller and liquid ghost-snare programming
Akai MPC60 / MPC2000 / MPC3000 — break slicing and the swing/sequencing engine for classic jungle-into-DnB production
E-mu SP-1200 / SP-12 / Drumulator — 12-bit resampling grit for gritty 'raw' and techstep-era kicks/snares
Elektron Machinedrum — mechanical, edited percussion loops and hat stutters for neurofunk
Roland TR-727 / TR-505 — congas and shakers for the liquid and jump-up palettes
Sonic Academy Kick 2 / modern synthesised kick design — the foghorn/jump-up era's from-scratch kick sound
